_comment: REASONING-GAP eval set for the stock graph (fwmhe8ysfrnx9fw7), authored 2026-06-13 to test LLM query rewrite (E11 follow-up to the dense-leg-vs-reasoning finding on #436). These are queries whose LITERAL surface topic differs from the asker's intent — answering requires an inference step ('powered up' -> electricity -> utilities), which similarity retrieval (lexical OR dense) does not do. The frozen dataset-stocks.json is mostly direct/paraphrase queries that already pass; this set deliberately probes the gap. Grades 0-3 (3=dedicated node, 2=strongly relevant, 1=marginal). qrels are title+excerpt-anchored (lighter than #223's pooled assessment — appropriate for a prototype set, not a frozen baseline). `rewrites` are precomputed keyword-rich rewrites simulating what an LLM rewrite step would emit; eval/rewrite-ab.js scores retrieval with the raw query (off) vs the rewrite (on). Run: STOCK_GID=fwmhe8ysfrnx9fw7.

queries.r1: which firms keep the AI server farms powered up
queries.r2: what stops a new AI data center from turning on
queries.r3: who benefits if AI needs far more electricity than planned
queries.r4: if one company could break the whole AI supply chain who is it
queries.r5: who makes money from the boring metal and wiring inside AI racks
queries.r6: what keeps a data center from overheating as the chips get hotter
queries.r7: companies that profit from AI's land and permit problem
queries.r8: who quietly profits when hyperscalers overspend on AI

rewrites.r1: data center energy and power suppliers: electric utilities, independent power producers, grid and transformers, natural gas turbines, nuclear, power distribution
rewrites.r2: AI data center buildout binding constraints: siting permitting and water, high-voltage switchgear and transformers, grid power, gas turbines
rewrites.r3: beneficiaries of rising AI electricity demand: regulated utilities, independent and merchant power producers, natural gas turbines, nuclear and uranium, grid equipment
rewrites.r4: single points of failure and choke points in the AI supply chain: TSMC foundry, ASML EUV monopoly, raw material and specialty gas concentration
rewrites.r5: components and materials inside AI server racks: connectors, active electrical cables, power distribution, specialty alloys, electrical interconnect
rewrites.r6: data center cooling: liquid cooling and thermal management for AI servers
rewrites.r7: data center siting, permitting, land and water constraints, and data center REITs
rewrites.r8: circular AI spending and vendor financing: capital circle, neoclouds, sovereign wealth funding, announced vs deployed capacity
